newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SEC urges Senate care if alter trading rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SEC urges Senate care if alter trading rules.

text.p: The Senate Agriculture Committee should take care to avoid damage to the cash and derivative markets in its attempts to update the Commodity Exchange Act, the chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a letter released Thursday.
SEC chairman Arthur Levitt cautioned against intruding on the Shad-Johnson Accord, which delineates jurisdiction of the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Levitt also said it would be helpful to provide more legal certainty for privately negotiated institutional transactions conducted over the counter.
A bill filed by committee leaders has language on that matter to codify exemptions from the CEA granted by CFTC.

"A better approach would be to exclude from the CEA privately negotiated institutional OTC transactions in securities-based swaps and all hybrid products that are not predominantly futures," Levitt wrote. "Thus, institutional OTC markets in securities products would be excluded from the CEA without regard to whether they might be viewed as futures."
Agriculture chairman Richard Lugar said Levitt's comments would be taken into consideration. An aide said the bill would provide certainty for legality of swaps.
